Edit an existing **standard invoice** by id. Send via `PUT /invoices/{id}` (or `POST /invoices/{id}`) with the full invoice payload — submitted line items, payments and custom fields replace the existing ones.

The invoice **cannot be edited** (returns 400 or 404) when it: is on a different branch than it was created on; has a valid (accepted) electronic invoice; has related credit charges, installment agreements or membership/credit renewals; falls in a closed financial period (non-draft); is tied to a closed POS shift; has a received requisition; or is selected in a production plan.

Requires edit permission — all-invoices edit access, or being the invoice's own staff with edit-own access.

The response is a **JSON array** with one result object per submitted invoice, in the same order as the request. A successful element carries the new invoice `id` and number; a failed element carries an error result with a message, so you must inspect each element to confirm it succeeded.

Per-element fields and defaulting behaviour are identical to **Add New Invoice** — see that endpoint for the full field reference.

get.description:
Updates an invoice's draft status.

Use `draft_status = 0` to **issue** a draft invoice — this assigns the official sequential invoice number and posts the invoice's payment journal entries. Use `draft_status = 1` to move an issued invoice **back to draft**, which removes those payment journal entries.

Requires permission to edit or issue invoices.

| `draft_status` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Issue the invoice (remove draft) |
| 1 | Set the invoice as draft |

The request is rejected with `400` when the change is not allowed — for example the invoice is already issued, it has completed payments (so it cannot be set back to draft), it has been refunded, or its date falls within a closed financial period.

parameters.description: Target draft state: `0` to issue, `1` to set as draft.

post.description:
Converts a sales order (identified by the `id` path parameter) into a new invoice.

The new invoice inherits the sales order's client, currency, shipping, discounts, adjustment, and a source link back to the sales order — these are taken from the sales order and **override** any values you send. Send `InvoiceItem` to choose which lines and quantities to convert (**partial conversion** is supported); you may also pass standard invoice fields such as `date`, `store_id`, or `draft`.

If the sales order has requisitions, conversion is limited to accepted/selected requisition lines — pass `requisition_ids[]` (query) to choose them when you hold the convert permission.

On success the invoice is created and returned with the standard creation envelope (HTTP `202` with the new invoice `id`). Requires the Sales Order module to be enabled and permission to create invoices / convert sales orders. The request is rejected with `404` when the sales order is missing, already invoiced, not permitted, or has no convertible items.

This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token. The response is a paginated collection (20 per page by default).

- **Pagination:** use `?page=<n>`. The response carries `current_page`, `last_page`, `per_page`, and `total`.

- **Sorting:** `sort[<field>]=asc|desc` (for example `sort[id]=desc`). When no `sort` is given the default order is `id` descending.
